This noise injection mechanism is designed to obscure sensitive information in the embeddings, thereby providing privacy guarantees while aiming to maintain the utility of the data. The authors leverage Rényi divergence and Bayesian Differential Privacy (BDP) to quantify the privacy protection offered by their method. The NVIB layer is trained to learn a noise model that is calibrated to the downstream task, which is a key aspect of the proposed approach. The empirical evaluation of NVDP is conducted on the GLUE benchmark, a collection of natural language processing tasks. The results demonstrate a trade-off between privacy and accuracy, showing that the model can maintain high utility with strong privacy guarantees at lower noise levels. The authors compare NVDP against a Vector-Space VIB (VTDP) baseline, showing that NVDP consistently achieves better privacy-utility trade-offs, particularly in terms of BDP and Rényi Divergence (RD) metrics. The paper provides a detailed explanation of the proposed method, including the mathematical foundations of the NVIB layer and the privacy guarantees offered by RDP and BDP. The authors also discuss the use of a denoising multi-head attention (MHA) layer to further enhance the performance of the model. Overall, the paper presents a significant contribution to the field of privacy-preserving machine learning, particularly in the context of transformer models. The integration of the NVIB layer within the transformer architecture and the use of nonparametric variational regularization for attention-based representations are novel aspects of this work. The empirical results on the GLUE benchmark provide evidence for the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving a balance between privacy and utility.
